channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Europe targets Uganda energy boost with fresh $33 million investment
item.description: The European Union has pledged €30 million, about $32.7 million, to support the rehabilitation of the Nalubaale-Kiira hydropower complex in Uganda, signalling a renewed push to strengthen the country’s energy infrastructure and economic growth.

item.title: South Africa's largest lenders raise $322 million in new bank loss-buffer issuance
item.description: South Africa’s largest banks have raised about $322 million in new loss-absorbing debt as part of a central bank framework designed to ensure troubled lenders can be recapitalised without relying on taxpayer bailouts.

item.title: South Africa’s first gold mine in 15 years clears key risk review for investors
item.description: A multidisciplinary due diligence review has strengthened investor confidence in the Qala Shallows gold project, positioning the development as a potential turning point for South Africa’s mining sector.

item.title: Top 10 best-governed countries in Africa, according to latest ranking (2026)
item.description: African countries are showing steady gains in political rights and press freedom, showing stronger democratic openness. However, weak rule of law and corruption control continue to limit overall governance performance across much of the continent.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the lowest IMF debt in February 2026
item.description: Recent involvement among African governments, foreign lenders, and global partners highlights the potential benefits of well-structured IMF programs for the continent.

item.title: Elon Musk escalates dispute with South Africa amid report of 14,000 illegal Starlink users, despite R500 million pledge
item.description: Despite a R500 million offer to connect 5,000 rural schools, Starlink remains unlicensed in South Africa. The standoff has escalated as 14,000 residents find ways to access the service anyway, putting Musk at odds with ICASA’s strict regulatory framework.

item.title: Africa’s largest diamond miner posts $511 million loss amid weak Chinese demand and U.S. tariff pressures
item.description: De Beers, Africa’s largest diamond miner, posted a sharply wider $511 million loss in 2025 as weak Chinese demand, U.S. tariff pressures and softer global prices weighed on its worldwide operations, including key mines in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa.

item.title: US tags Ivory Coast travel risk zone, warns visitors to stay alert
item.description: The U.S. Department of State has reissued a Level 2 travel advisory for Côte d’Ivoire, urging visitors to “exercise increased caution” due to persistent security risks.

item.title: US troops arrive in northeast Nigeria as counterterror push intensifies
item.description: About 100 United States military personnel have arrived in northeast Nigeria to support training and intelligence operations, signalling a renewed phase in security cooperation between Abuja and Washington as the country confronts an expanding insurgency.

item.title: Top 10 African countries that attracted China’s $66.1 billion energy financing [2000-2024]
item.description: Between 2000 and 2024, China channelled $66.1 billion into Africa’s energy sector, financing power plants, oil and gas projects, transmission infrastructure, and renewable energy developments across the continent.
